newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar ends flat after lackluster jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar ends flat after lackluster jobs data.

text.p: * The Canadian dollar ended flat at C$1.3502 (US$0.7406) on Friday from Thursday's close at C$1.3501 (US$0.7406) after lackluster Canadian jobs data * Canada's unemployment rate was unchanged at 9.7 percent in January from December as the economy created only 5,100 new jobs * Canada unit seen trading between C$1.3450 and C$1.3520 in near term.

The Canadian unemployment rate remained flat at 9.7 percent in January, while employment growth rate for the same month showed a small jump of 5,100 jobs. A Reuters survey of economists had predicted an unemployment rate of 9.6 percent.

"I think if you look at the headline numbers, it may seem a bit disappointing with only minor job gains of around 5,000. But if you scratch the surface and look a little deeper, you see that this report is not that tepid," said Canada Trust economist Steve Saldanha.
The numbers also showed a gain of 32,000 full-time jobs which, economists said, will help boost consumer confidence.
The Canadian currency was expected to trade between C$1.3450 and C$1.3520 in the near term, traders said.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar strengthened to 1.2307 marks on Friday from 1.2238 marks on Thursday, but slipped to 91.19 yen from 91.63 on Thursday.
